text_fidelity_a:
Passnag Light Saber with 3 Mode Sound, Force Heavy Dueling, FX Real RGB 12 Colors Changeable Light Saber with Blaster Sound, Metal Hilt with 1' Blade--Black SN227B [[VIDEOID:70401b9086e08489b8471006d9a7ceb7]] March 2, 2021 UPDATE:
--------------------------
This was adult owned and taken care of. Mainly used for display, and sparingly demo'ed in the 6 months that I've owned it. I hadn't turned it on for a long while, probably several months. I decided to test it out again, and it wouldn't turn on. I've charged it for over 5 hours. There is a red light to indicate it's charging, but still won't turn on. No longevity for this item. Reducing review to 1-star.

Original Review:
------------------
Very fun light saber! Has a good heft to it and feels high quality. The handle is some sort of aluminum or metal. This looks much better than those plasticky toys. But as usual, with all these sabers on the market, the worst looking part is the the plastic tube. Our tech isn't there yet, but hopefully one day, we can get rid of that plastic tube and have a real solid light beam out! In any case, here are the controls:

-Single click button once to turn on.
-Single click button again to hear effect.
-While it's on, Double click for a blasting sound which the manual calls "lockup mode." It will stay at this sound until you Double Click again to get out of it.
-While it's on, triple click to change colors (this is finicky though)
-Press & hold button to turn off.
-To change the sound "theme," while it's off, hold the button, you will hear a sound theme. Hold the button again to hear the next sound theme, hold it again to hear the next, etc. There is a total of 4 themes, one of which is actually mute.
-To use any of these themes, once you like what you hear, just single click the button to turn on and play. Remember clicking once turns it on, but holding the button would cause it to cycle through the themes. But once on, to get back to cycling through the themes, you need to press & hold to turn off first, then press & hold to cycle through the themes.

My kids have a few sabers from the out of business toy store. This one belongs to daddy. LOL! I'm knocking 1 star for the finicky controls and instructions that were a little hard to figure out. 4 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Passnag Light Saber with 3 Mode Sound, Force Heavy Dueling, FX Real RGB 12 Colors Changeable Light Saber with Blaster Sound, Metal Hilt with 1' Blade--Black SN227B

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO NINJAGO Spinjitzu Slam Kai vs Samurai 70684 Building Kit (164 Pieces) Kiddo had fun building it (he's 7) but there is no guidance on what you actually do with it. "No rules, no limits" is the Lego description of what comes next, so I guess he just does whatever. I would have been better to suggest a base game, and then hint at ways to improve of make your own. As it is, they seem to have taken the easy way out with no real end plan in the guise of "imaginary play". Kid liked building it, and the cats were highly entertained chasing the tops. But with no real structured game at the end he sorta lost interest.

Older kids might be able to come up with more fun things to do with it on their own. Mine was looking for the rules and how to "win", then disappointed there wasn't any.

text_fidelity_a:
Radio Flyer Ultimate EZ Folding Wagon for kids and cargo, Red, Model Number: 3900 The foldable flyer is so far so good--easily put together, nicely constructed, easily foldable and relatively compact.

Packaging: It comes in a large box already folded. Separate parts are minimal: the canopy (folded), the handle, two wheels packed separately with their screws, the four rods that hold up the canopy. Everything is clearly packaged, plastic is wrapped with very easily removable tape, several soft cushions protect from banging/scratches. Took about a two minutes to pull everything out and remove them from their bags.

Assembly: You need a phillips screwdriver and a wrench. From already having the parts out of their bags and laid out to completely done and mobile took exactly 14 minutes. It’s an extremely easy, simple, and fast assembly.
1) Pull up on the handles to unfold the wagon
2) Press down on the middle panel to snap into rigidity
3) Attach the two separated wheels, each of which is labeled L or R accordingly (the label is sort of a raised letter--black on black--you may need to look closely at the wheel strut to see it. Attaching the wheels consists of dropping the wagon atop the wheel struts, placing a washer and screw, and tightening. Simple, fast, easy.
4) attach the handle--one bolt and nut. Simple, fast, easy
5) Push the four rods into the holes for the canopy and press down
6) Attach the canopy via four snaps onto the top of the rods

The holes/snaps all lined up perfectly. There was no difficulty, no manipulation, no cursing. All as easy as could be.

To fold, simply remove the canopy and lift up the center panel. Again, worked flawlessly.

It’s a mix of plastic and fabric. But the plastic doesn’t feel cheap and the fabric seem pretty rugged. Overall build quality seems solid and as if it will last through the years with little kids.

It moves smoothly and easily. It’s very light and maneuverable. The handle is not adjustable, but it does allow you to contract it for storage. There are cup holders on either side of the inside and cup holders on the outside end at the handle.

The seats have a “seat belt”. They cannot be removed, nor do they fold flat. The canopy is a nice touch for shade and rain (though it won’t stop kids getting wet if there’s any wind slanting the rain).

Really, there’s nothing at all to complain about. If you don’t mind the price, this is an excellent and convenient pick-up
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer Ultimate EZ Folding Wagon for kids and cargo, Red, Model Number: 3900

Adora My Cuddle & Coo Baby “Cuppy Cake” - Touch Activated Doll with 5 Sounds: She Cries, Coos, Giggles, Kisses Back & Says Momma Just like I had thought before actually receiving this, you are probably thinking that this is a hefty pricetag for a doll that doesn't even have the American Girl logo attached to it... well, move over Pleasant Company (yeah, I said it), because Adora is a new generation of dolls that are not only kid approved (my girls, ages ranging from 6-10, all love their Adora dolls) but it is also parent/caregiver/teacher approved (I would know, as I'm technically all 3, haha). My girls love this doll because she's so cuddly and lifelike, and I love her because I have spent some time actually researching the Adora company... and let me just say THANK YOU for finally coming out with a line of dolls that are crafted from SAFE and nontoxic materials! No more feeling that tiny pang of worry ("mom guilt" lol) whenever my daughter is snuggled up with her doll. I love the peace of mind that comes from knowing the dolls arms, legs, and face are made of vinyl and are BPA free. Finally, a toy company with ethics!

Many of Adoras dolls are machine washable (this particular one has electronics and therefore is not, so care must be taken when wiping the vinyl parts and perhaps spraying a safe vinegar solution on the dolls plush core to keep clean and fresh). Honestly, I can't really comment on the electronic aspect of this doll, as I turned off that feature pretty early (i think it encourages better open-ended imaginative play that way... not to mention less annoying for cranky mommies lol). So you'll have to check other reviews for better details on that function.

All in all, yes, this is not a cheap doll. But in my humble opinion, you are getting a lot of value for your money with this doll. The brand has less expensive plush options too that are just as adorable, less expensive, and even machine washable (we have one and I'll be doing a review soon). The Adora line has a wide selection of dolls and accessories too by the way. I'm actually excited to buy some accessories because I feel like they are very competitively priced and plus it feels good to support such an ethical company that brings so much joy to children.

Grandparents, this is a gift that will not only make you the favorite grandparent, but will also please even the pickiest of health-conscious daughter-in-laws lol.

Two thumbs up for Adora!!
text_fidelity_b: Adora My Cuddle & Coo Baby “Cuppy Cake” - Touch Activated Doll with 5 Sounds: She Cries, Coos, Giggles, Kisses Back & Says Momma

I need to use it for a party next weekend, so I purchased a different one with metal clamps - and having major problems with the new one as well. I would say..... if you need it for a one time use, it's still worth it, but a huge a disappointment that it can't be used again. The balloon stands are still fine.

Original review: I used this arch for my niece's baby shower. I was seriously worried about the stability of the arch, setup, and tear down. But after giving it a test run at my house first, it was so simple to set up and use, and it was very stable. I received a bunch of clips with the set, but I found that putting the balloons around the pole was much easier than using the clips. We also purchased 2 sets of balloon poles, and those were easy to use as well, same method. I took these on a plane across the country, and they traveled well. The only negative, and it is minor, was that there were no instructions included in the boxes. I initially had a hard time getting the poles to stay together, until I YouTubed a Party Zealot setup video, then it became apparent what the glue dots are for! Trust me...you will want to use the glue dots to "glue" the poles together, or they WILL come apart. But using the glue dots made them much more stable. There are still some little blue clippy things that came in the boxes that we never did figure out how to use, and I couldn't find the information anywhere on their website or google searches. So they remain a mystery. But overall, for the money, this was a HUGE success and a fantastic buy. I have never had so many compliments. Highly recommend.

Craft-tastic – String Art Kit – Craft Kit Makes 2 Large String Art Canvases – Desserts Edition I picked up this set for my 6yo and she loved it. Even though she is fiercely independent and incredibly artistic, this was a too difficult for her to do on her own. Her hand-eye coordination isn't developed enough yet to push 75+ pins in place, so I ended up having to do most of that step for her. I also had to help her with keeping the string taunt. But with that said, I had a heck of lot fun doing it with her. She's never done string art before and I haven't in years, and we both really enjoyed doing the turtle together (we'll save the flower for later). She was so proud of it once we were finished.
So yeah, I would recommend this set. It's good quality and comes with plenty of extra supplies (like enough string). And seeing as how it took it us well over an hour to do, I think it's a good value. And that's important to me, because I can't tell you how many times I've spent $10 or $15 on an art kit just for her to finish in a matter of minutes. But as I mentioned before, this was to difficult for my first grader to do on her own. I think this is more suited to a pre-teen and it would make a fantastic gift.

text_fidelity_a:
Munchkin Years ago while talking about games one person commented that a certain game was a perfect "beer and pretzels" game. The game in question was simple to play, had lots of off-color humor and while it clearly did not take itself all that seriously, was seriously fun. His comment started a converation about what other games might fit that category.

Munchkin could be the sibling to those old games. Even in this first set, the puns are everywhere and the game is more about having fun and socailizing than winning. Sure it almost requires that you backstab each other freely, but its also the kind of fast paced and humorous game that keeps the players from becoming too serious about what's happening. The idea is to have fun, winning is just a bonus.

The humor can be crude and a bit adult, but other than that Munchkin has proved to be a great game.

Another reviewer commented that this may be due to craft stores experiencing a lot of shoplifting - but the book could have been easily secured using double sided tape or light adhesive.

Other than that, this kit will provide hours of enjoyment for adults and kids, especially those (like me) suffering from cabin fever thanks to an interminably long winter. I would definitely buy more as gifts if it were less than the current price.

UGears Models 3-D Wooden Puzzle - Mechanical Horse Mechanoid This horse is striking in appearance. It looks wild and spirited. It is quite a conversation piece on its looks alone. I would give it five stars alone for that. Movement is not as spectacular, but it does move. There’s a winding key and start/stop control levers. The horse is not able to take more than 5 steps without halting or simply falling over. It looks like the last motions of a horse before succumbing to the effects of a trank dart. The kit is a real bear to assemble. The instructions must be heeded. You may find you have to flip ahead a few pages at times to see just what this subassembly is that you are working on and where it is supposed to go. I knew at the start that I would need to sand the pieces and use the provided wax. Ther's not a whole lot of wax. It’s a 1 inch slice of a candle but the important thing is that it enough for the horse. The wax is somewhat soft, like beeswax. I had no problem with missing pieces. There are six boards with laser cut parts. If you don't see anything missing, you have all the parts. Assembly is a bit tedious and somewhat painful. As the model continues to take shape and become more horse-like there is the adrenalin surge all model builders feel when they are nearing the end. Once assembly is completed the key is wound and switch is moved. My model just sat there. C’mon little horsy, let’s go. Well, back-winding the key overcomes the initial friction and horse begins to haltingly show movement. Lots of going back and forth with the key helps to distribute the wax and the horse becomes more limber. After lots of massaging like this you can get the horse to take 4 or maybe 5 steps. Max is 9 and only rarely achieved. It will usually fall over to announce it is finished walking. Well and good. It is still a cool model and I would build one again. I’m giving it 5 stars but 4 would be reasonable too. I wish it walked a bit better and that the instructions had a bit of expository text. This is a worthwhile model that will occupy 8 hours of your life in assembly. It is ingenious.

I have a few hints on this horse:
Mine locked up once while fully wound up. I could not get it to operate at all. I tried moving the legs and rapping the body with my knuckles. Nothing! My horse was dead. It was not until I grasped the horses neck and moved it forward and back that the gears unlocked. This only happened once, but it was super frustrating as I was contemplating opening up the entire model to fix it.

Understand at the outset that this horse can’t walk for long. If you watch the clever videos the horse appears to leave its stall and seems to be on a journey to a pasture or whatever. If you look closely the horse only takes a few steps in each scene. Clever editing makes it look like the horse can go on a pastoral journey. Not really complaining because all the ad copy and literature says the horse can’t go far. This is only a problem if your expectations are too high and unrealistic. It is what it is, a model of mechanical horse. So enjoy that as I do I.

My rubber band broke. I suppose it had a nick in it that grew over time. I was able to cut out the broken piece and retie the rubber band but it is not easy working in the body of the assembled model. So do examine the length of the rubber band before assembly.

Update on the rubber band issue 5 days later:
The rubber band broke again. No, I haven’t over wound it. I’ll have to see if I can get a replacement from somewhere.

The rubber bands for the horse’s mane and tail are genius. Looks great and the bands lie perfectly when cut. I was worried I’d need hair styling skills to make the horse look good. It was no problem.

Seriously, sand everything. Knock down the edges of the large pieces as well so they lose their painful sharpness. If you have to reach into the interior of the model later you will be glad you did.

Some parts are seeming impossible to press together with human hands. I finally resorted to a small furniture clamp with soft jaws to supplement my finger strength. I think pliers or small c-clamp would work, as well.

A cushiony work surface was helpful in supporting a board while I was breaking a part loose from the board. I used towel I use for assembly projects.

It really takes 8 uninterrupted hours to assemble this model no matter how skilled you think you are. If you leave out trying to be extra careful and the extra sanding I guess you could do it in about five.

On page 13 of the instructions I was confused. The diagram seems to suggest that the rubber band should be folded upon itself in thirds. After puzzling on this I covinced myself that doubling the band was correct and it turned out to be right choice.

Check for proper operation of parts during assembly. In some steps you are "told" to operate the key and check that the parts move freely. This is very important. Once the horse is fully assembled getting back inside it is a difficult task since gear timing must be maintained.

There is a down side to using the wax. Your hands will get a coating of wax and when that is transferred to the horse there will be discolored spots. Try to keep the wax from where you don't want the wood to darken. I washed my hands frequently and still ended up with a horse that is more pinto than wood white.

There are no troubleshooting hints in the instructions. If you can't find help on the website you are on your own. I do have a vibe from Ugears that they are helpful and I think you can correspond with them and get help if you have a bad problem.
text_fidelity_b: UGears Models 3-D Wooden Puzzle - Mechanical Horse Mechanoid

Faber-Castell How to Rainbow Watercolor Pencils Set - Kids Painting Kits, Art Kit for Kids 6-8+ At the time of this review, this set is under $10. If it were over $10, I would probably subtract a star. This is definitely beginner, student quality.
But if you have a child, or maybe you are just looking for something reasonably priced to see if you enjoy sketching, even though it's geared for children, this set can't be beat.

The main reason it gets five stars, is that you get four different hardness levels of graphite pencils. Perfect for experimenting with your creativity and making a sketch come alive. And it's less messy than charcoal sticks, so once again, it's the perfect introduction to nurture a child's creativity and talent.
To make it even better, there's a little pamphlet to encourage and explain how to get your feet wet. I really like that the emphasis is on the fact that there are no mistakes, that each line is is just fine. So important for children that might be discouraged that they aren't instantly a great artist, forgetting or not understanding that being an artist is only 10% talent and 90% learning and desire.
It might be only a folded over page, but it covers various techniques. All is written in a way that kids and young adults can easily follow. This set is cured for ages 7 and up.
And once again, a 7-year-old doesn't need professional quality pencil sharpeners or paper. You can see in the photograph how thin the paper pages are, and how cheesy the little pencil sharpener is. Cheesy, but perfect for the purpose.

This well thought out set is just what I would expect from Farber-Castell. Their supplies are favored by the students and professionals worldwide.

I hope that this review has helped you to make a decision about whether or not this set is right for you or a special child. Kids seem to be passionate about something one minute, and totally change the next. This little set is a very small investment, but of course, little investments add up.

City Fire Station Building Blocks Set W/ Fire Truck, Fire Rescue Helicopter, Drone & Fire Engine Toys, Fire Command Center Playset, Firefighters Roleplay Toy Gifts for Kids Boys Girls Ages 6+ (744PCS) It's fake LEGO. It may pretend it isn't, but it is,
As well as being fake LEGO it has one other claim to fame.
It is very disappointing.
When companies copy (not be inspired by. I am all for being inspired! this is copying) because of patents, they cannot copy the construct of the bricks. So they end up with bricks that do not push together well, giving models less resilience to being knocked over, picked up or even played with.
Except for the tile pieces. They stick like they were coated in gorilla glue! You may need power tools to get them apart.

Aside from the poor quality of the bricks, what else can be said? Nothing good, sadly. The set designs are primitive. The vehicles are not all on the same scale. Some will not hold the minifigs.
The accessories are another disappointment. Ugly, hard for the minifigs to hold.

If you have a nephew or niece who loves LEGO, and you simply cannot stand this family member, you have found the perfect gift.

Otherwise, keep looking. You will pay more for LEGO, and it is worth every cent!
text_fidelity_b: City Fire Station Building Blocks Set W/ Fire Truck, Fire Rescue Helicopter, Drone & Fire Engine Toys, Fire Command Center Playset, Firefighters Roleplay Toy Gifts for Kids Boys Girls Ages 6+ (744PCS)

I’ll start with my main complaint with these first. These are dark cards, using a dark gray background for all suits, and using a dark purple for spades and clubs. This creates a low-contrast scheme that is more difficult to see in low light, and is less than pleasant even in brighter light. This is an unfortunate choice that could have been handled better. The artwork on these is impressive. A good bit of detail went into each design and it shows. The number cards (2 -10) have small designs on them that are at times hard to see and look at without a magnifying glass, though.

This are well made cards, coated and designed so they will not stick together even in damp climates. They come in a beautiful tuck box with reflective highlights in purple.

These are not bad cards at all. They’re beautiful and they’re well made, and they have some incredible artwork. However, the color scheme is not the best and these cards would be even better if the background and black suit colors were chosen a little more thoughtfully.

text_fidelity_a:
Boom Boom Balloon, Exciting Anticipation Family Board Game Outdoor Summer Toy, for Kids Ages 8 and up My oldest son(5) recently started daily injections. As you would expect, he hates them. We try to do something fun after each of them, and this was used as one of his "surprises". It did the trick and took his mind off that mean needle.

This game is really fun! Not only did my children enjoy it, but I did, too. It does come with a few issues, though.

First of all, as I put the thing together, the instructions say to never use your mouth to blow up the balloon. You must use a balloon pump. A balloon pump isn't included, so I chose to use my mouth to blow up the balloon, since I had excited children waiting to play. It went fine. I was able to blow up the balloon while it was in the frame without any problem.

Secondly, we couldn't get the top clip piece to stay put. There's a clip that holds the 3 pieces of the frame together at the top. It kept coming lose no matter how tight I tried to get it. When I took the thing apart, I couldn't get one frame piece to come apart. So, 2 were so lose the whole thing kept coming apart, but one was so tight I had to put it in the box together, and therefore, couldn't close the lid.

Third, one of the sticks was broke within minutes of playing the game. Thankfully, there are 4 extras included, so we can still play. Plus, the recommended age is 8 and up. I played this game with my 2 and 5 year olds. The 2 year old is the one that broke the stick, so I'm not taking stars off for that issue or anything. It's simply to warn you that they do break pretty easily.

There are 12 balloons included. They are all the same: blue, with a face. They are the regular sized balloons, so I imagine this game will work perfectly fine with store bought replacement balloons. You just probably won't have a face on there.

I know it sounds like a lot of complaining up there, but we really enjoyed this game!

The basics: You put the thing together, which is really simple. You put the balloon in the frame, blow it up, and then wrap it around the "hook" at the bottom to keep the air in without having to actually tie it. Super simple. You take the sticks and put them in the holes(6) until you hear the first click. Then you take turns rolling dice. Whatever number it lands on is the amount of times you push in a stick. It can be the same stick or one click each on different sticks. Whoever pops the balloon first loses(or wins if you're my children).

Overall, it's a fun game that's worth the issues that come with it.
text_fidelity_b: Boom Boom Balloon, Exciting Anticipation Family Board Game Outdoor Summer Toy, for Kids Ages 8 and up

Lucky Ducks - The Memory and Matching Game That Moves - Includes A Fun Pop The Pig Make-A-Match Card Game The only bad thing about this game is the fact that my 2 year thinks it's a radio. We've had it for about a month now, and as I write this, it's "playing" in the background. It's playing in the background almost every night, if not during the day, too. It's super annoying! :P It's supposed to sound like ducks, I guess, but it's just lots of squeaking.

Otherwise, it's super cute, and my boys love playing it. I think 2-4 year old children will enjoy it the most, but it's labeled 3 and up. I imagine this is due to the stickers that must go on the ducks, and game board(which is a motorized pond). You do need batteries! There are 4 colors of stickers, 4 each. 3 of each will go on ducks and 1 on the game board. I wasn't paying attention enough to realize one of each color went on the game board. I ended up having to peel some stickers off of ducks.

You put the ducks on the game board, assign a color to each child(up to 4 players), and then press the center button. The ducks will then circle around the pond. Taking turns the child picks up a duck and turns it over. If it matches their assigned color, they keep it. If not, they put it back on the pond. While all the ducks are on the pond, it's a little crowded, so it was tough for my 2 year old to get the duck placed back on there without knocking over another duck, or several. It's easier to turn the pond off while your child is looking at the color and placing it back on the pond.

Overall, this is a fun game to teach a few colors, along with the art of taking turns and patience. My children had so much fun with it, they were impatient for their turn.

NKOK RC Sonic SSAS R2 Car with Lights, Blue (614) This NKOK RC Sonic SSAS R2 Car with Lights was a gift for my son on his 7th birthday. He is all about Sonic the Hedgehog right now. I'm not sure where he saw it, but all of a sudden he wants nothing but Sonic. However, Sonic isn't really popular right now. There is the pending "live-action" Sonic movie, but that has been pushed back from November to Winter/Spring of 2020 so any tie-in toys will also probably be pushed back. So, this RC car was the only thing I could really find that wasn't exorbitantly priced.

This currently priced at $27, but I would say it's really not worth more than $20. It's really light weight and does not come with batteries. So, keep that in mind when you are giving this as a gift. The car and the remote both need batteries. AA and AAA. Sonic is part of the car. He does not come out. And this operates just like any other R/C car. There's nothing special about it other than it is Sonic. The headlights turn on when going forward and turn off when in reverse. My so has launched this off the porch and into the front yard several times. It's only about 6 inches down from the porch to the ground, so I doubt there's any real damage, but I would caution against doing that from any heights above that. However, I would say that he has played with this for a couple minutes and then moved onto something else. Without any other bells and whistles, the hold factor for this toys wasn't very long. Keep in mind while my son loves Sonic, he doesn't play the video games or do much on electronic devices. So, he actually plays with toys most of his day.

So, I think this is a nice, cute gift, but I think it is a bit over priced.
text_fidelity_b: NKOK RC Sonic SSAS R2 Car with Lights, Blue (614)

If you choose to use it as a birthday train, just to warn you, the candle doesn't stay in place like it should. Each block has a hole in the back of it. text_fidelity_a: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath This is a perfect addition to the Fall basket. There are always lots of books about squirrels and acorns to add to the fall line-up and this game goes with them well. It's a great companion to those books and we've all had fun with it. There's also a little puzzle to go with the game, which adds more fun to the squirrel/acorn focus. To play the game, the players take turns rolling a die. The color/number that is rolled is what color and how many(up to 2) acorns you put into Charlie's mouth. Once he gets full, the acorns roll out the holes that are in the tree trunk that Charlie stands on. Using only one hand, the players race to collect the acorns. The first player to fill up their acorn stash card wins. The rules say that if a player rolls a certain color and it's not in the main stash of acorns, that player has to take one of their collected acorns or take one from another player. Taking from another player won't be for all families, but it can be adapted, if desired. Also, with the acorns rolling everywhere, it's tricky finding the best place to play. The acorns will roll off the table, but if on the floor, they could roll under things, like couches, if it's a smaller space. Our home is small, so we try to put up little "walls" to make sure the acorns don't roll under things. Overall, it's a fun game and the quality of it is nice, too. It's a simple game that's a great way to add a bit of joy to a day.

BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer) Mattel has brought a new world to target practice and just plain fun with soft dart guns with this BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster. With no batteries required, the fun is endless. Instead of batteries to power the gun, it is air powered. You have to pump the gun to get enough air pressure to fire the soft darts. Mattel states the gun is for ages 6 and up, but this gun is on the heavy side and requires a bit of strength just to pump it, so I feel ages 7 and up would be a better fit. Even though our 6 year old neighbor didn't want to put this gun down, it was difficult for him to pump it for firing.

The gun is very sturdy being large and made of a heavy plastic. I can see this gun lasting quite a bit of use and not ending up in the trash for a long while. Once pumped it is easy to fire, whether firing one dart or the entire 20 dart clip. At the end of the gun is a special shield you can open up to not only protect yourself from oncoming darts, but your opponents darts will actually stick to this protective shield, allowing you to capture his darts.

Besides the gun there are 30 Smart Stick darts, a 20 dart clip and a Smart Stick target included. The target is great for improving your aim, especially firing one dart at a time. The 20 dart clip is really fun, whether firing at the target or your opponent, as it fires all 20 darts in a matter of a few seconds. It literally fires up to 50 feet, as we shot all 20 darts and several darts went well over 45 feet away. The rapid fire at such a distance is really a lot of fun for the backyard.

Even though these darts are really soft plastic, you will find out that once the children find out how much fun it is to shoot darts at both the target and each other, you may want to purchase the safety eye gear. I don't know if having all 20 darts coming at you from 50 feet away would need some type of eye protection, but I feel it's better to have some type of eye gear on. There is no doubt, this is a safe, sturdy toy with your children wanting to run around and play with this outdoors, gives it 5 Stars. Just getting the kids off the couch away from video games makes it a 5 Star toy, as the exercise alone is worth 5 Stars.
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Ben Franklin Toys Electronic Bill & Coin Counter Bank with LCD Screen, One Size This is a really great idea for a children's bank and the top part, the counter, works really well. Unfortunately, there are a number of things here that made it not really work for my family. At least not at this time.

First, with little children in the house, the top buttons get pressed accidentally or on purpose when they are not supposed to and so the count has not been correct for that reason. I almost would've preferred some other method of managing bills and kept this as a coin counter only so that you have the immediate feedback putting something in, seeing the number change, and knowing that it's accurate. This would not be an issue in households only with bigger kids who can control themselves from pushing buttons inappropriately, but definitely made it not workable in my house during these years.

Next, I really hoped that the cool top would have threads so that they could fit on a mason jar of any size, so while the little ones are tiny they can have a little chart, and as they grow older they can have a large jar, but unfortunately it does not work with any size mason jar – the sizing, the threads, and the lip that hangs over are all totally different.

Lastly, and this is my main issue, the cheap, foggy, and unattractive plastic container that holds all of the money is so lightweight and is angled weird so that if there are primarily bills with only a few coins in there, the whole thing gets really top-heavy and wants to tip over. My son primarily gets money through finding change on the ground and through getting dollars or 20s on his birthday or Christmas. So there are a few coins in there, sure, but mostly single bills sent from afar through the mail. Had they made the top interchangeable with Mason jars, this would have been an issue because I just would put the whole thing on nice glass mason jar, probably one of those colored blue, purple, or green ones that they've come out with in recent years. Alas, you're really stuck with just the plastic container that the lid fits on. This limits how long anybody would want to use something like this, because I think most teenagers have slightly better taste than to want some cheap plastic thing of a single specific size sitting in their bedroom.

That said, for a very specific age range and if you don't have smaller children around the house, this could work really well and be a very fun way of having kids learn about saving and making it rewarding.
text_fidelity_b: Ben Franklin Toys Electronic Bill & Coin Counter Bank with LCD Screen, One Size

text_fidelity_a:
Minsk Remote Control Stunt Car Toy, 4WD RC Cars Double Sided Rotating Vehicles 360° Flips to Bloom, 2.4GHz High Speed Rechargeable Toy Presents for 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 Year Old Boy Birthday The car itself is pretty cool. I like the way it moves its entire axels to do its stunts. You can get a pretty good idea of hwo this moves if you look at the pictures. Simple, but effective. Seems like kids younger than 8 would like this; odd because they show small kids crawling on the floor using this, but say it is for ages 8 and up. Just watch they don't try to eat the batteries, I guess. It's not super fast, either, so older kids might get bored.

Anyway, they totally cheaped out on the battery setup. 400mAh?!?! Are you kidding me? Even the cheap, "included" versions of decent brands are 1100mAh, with good ones getting 2500mAh or more. And why the goofy charging setup? You have to take it out and then hook it to an oddball USB cable (so now you can't just use any USB cable you have laying around, you have to have this one on hand). They should just wire a higher capacity battery inside and add a micro-USB port like everybody else. And maybe similar functionality for the controller, which, oddly, uses two batteries...more than the car itself.

Pretty fun. Not well thought out overall, but on the other hand, if your kids falls out of love with toys quickly, maybe it's better not to spend more for the battery setup that could have been...
text_fidelity_b: Minsk Remote Control Stunt Car Toy, 4WD RC Cars Double Sided Rotating Vehicles 360° Flips to Bloom, 2.4GHz High Speed Rechargeable Toy Presents for 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 Year Old Boy Birthday

My 3 and 5 year old can just grab themselves a project and work on them together. Sometimes I've helped, but other times not. It's a great way to teach a little independence, and give this mama a moment of peace. ;) It's also been great for organizing projects for my 3 year old to work on while his older brothers do schoolwork. My goal has been to simplify for more peace, and this little kit has been a blessing in that goal.

Of course, you can use the portfolio to organize finished projects, but I typically throw stuff like this in the garbage after the newness has worn off. I only keep the more original, creative things my children create, and these project aren't original or overly creative. Sometimes easy projects like this are just what a child(and mommy/daddy/other person in charge) needs, though, and I appreciate having them around.

As far as art projects, you'll get 12 separate pages. Some are for coloring, some for putting stickers on, and many of them are sticky pages. (You'll pull paper off, leaving a sticky part. It will hold paper or shapes or buttons without the worry and mess of glue.) It also comes with various shapes and sizes of paper for sticking on pages, colors, buttons, and stickers. *Note: In one of the other kits from Alex Jr., the whole sticky part came off while trying to pull the paper off. My kids were disappointed, but that page can then just be used as a sticker page or coloring page. My youngest two highly prefer the sticky pages, though!

Overall, this is a nice kit! It's been a blessing to have a few "busy" projects around.

Green Toys Build-a-Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset - BPA Free, Phthalates Free, Creative Play Toys for Gross Motors, Fine Motor Skill Development. Toys and Games Green Toys Build a Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset is a toy made with greenness in mind. It is manufactured with recycled materials and is great for environmentally- conscious parents who wants their kids to have some creative fun while also minimizing environmental impact. Designed for children between the ages of three and six, it is one of the few building toys that doesn't involve blocks or other interlocking rectangular pieces.

This toy involves building arrangements of flowers on a green, branch like base and there is no end to the different number of creative arrangements that kids can make. The pieces consist of leaves and three different flowers and they can be stacked and arranged in any number of ways. The combinations are endless and every time my girls play, it turns into a new adventure. My girls love creative toys, flowers, and art, so a toy like this is very likeable and enjoyable to them.

I like that this toy is made using recycled materials and I like the small, cube- shaped box included for storage. Most manufacturers do not even think about including a small storage box, and this often forces parents to use plastic bags or plastic containers to store the pieces. With an included box, there is no need to reach for these environmentally- unfriendly storage receptacles that may one day wind up in a landfill. Instead, you just use the included box, which is also made from recycled material, and the pieces will be safe to use for the next adventure.

With its lack of batteries, green composition, and creative encouragement, this toy is certainly a nice change from most others, but does it have any possible flaws or potential issues? I can think of only a few. One is the small pieces. They can easily become misplaced, so parents need to watch closely to make sure that kids place all of the pieces back into the box. Of course, the nice fact here is that you can afford to lose a few because, since they are all interchangeable, it won't prevent the toy from being used again and again. Another issue is that this toy could become boring after a while. There are those youngsters who crave action, lights, and sounds in their toys and if yours is one of them, then they may grow tired of the toy in a short time.

Recycling is certainly a good idea and creative toys that require imagination and not so much of the lights and sounds so common with kids' toys today are definitely a nice change of pace. Green Toys Build a Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset is a very nice little toy from Green Toys and it makes a great choice for these reasons. The possible building combinations are endless and while some kids may tire of it in a short time, it still has enough positive qualities and creative entertainment value to make it worth a purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Green Toys Build-a-Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset - BPA Free, Phthalates Free, Creative Play Toys for Gross Motors, Fine Motor Skill Development. Toys and Games

The secret to the black mold: Take apple cider vinegar and test one of the squirts that the paint (looks like paint, but my grandson doesn't put these in his mouth) and fill it with some apple cider vinegar and shake it around. Repeat, but don't squirt it all out. If you already have mold, the children's health is more important. Through them out and for a few dollars, buy knew ones and keep on top of the cleaning. You can keep the cider vinegar in the garage if that's where all you swim gear gets dumped out when you come home and just take care of it right away. I hope this helps!
